title: Wire application Queue Fabric admission, durable journal and restart replay
summary: Candidate3 local qualification shows permanent Queue Fabric delivery recovery and independent admission-journal replay, including idempotency for requestId across delivery ids, conflict rejection and terminal evidence recording. It does NOT yet qualify live app activation.
requirements: Exactly five command fields: contract, requestId, artifactDigest, artifactRef, target. Reject unknown fields; do not silently accept older wire.application.deploy/0.1 candidate manifest commands.
Canonical lowercase sha256:64-hex digest, storage-fabric:// protected artifact reference, bounded token requestId and target. Verifier must separately authenticate producer and target policy.
Use the existing authorised ObjectQueueManager with a PERMANENT persistent delivery queue, not a second manager.

Persist WAPP_ADMIT in a separate QueueDurableStore STRICT ledger before ACK; on failure RELEASE for retry; same requestId + same immutable digest/ref/target becomes DUPLICATE_REQUEST; conflicting reuse becomes REJECTED_REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT.
Pending accepted requests survive process restart until a trusted worker attaches evidence to WAPP_COMPLETE; journal status is not live HTTPS probe itself.
One writer per journal root is required pending a distributed fencing lease. Close-on-append and STRICT replay do not establish physical fsync/power-loss durability.
Do not classify installation as PROBED_ACTIVE unless an independently authenticated HTTPS/WebSocket/browser semantic live probe succeeds.

qualification.scope: Local native acceptance; not production web/session qualification

outstanding: Authenticated Ed25519 .wapp verifier and Storage Fabric immutable download
Single active writer distributed lease and split-brain fencing
Real public HTTPS/TLS + WSS semantic action/observation round-trip
Generation drain and rollback with active sessions
